one_line_contribution: A factorial ALFWorld experiment that crosses the retrieval query key (goal sentence vs. initial observation vs. stall observation) with the rate at which scene-keyed object-location bindings are planted into the bank (0/25/50/100 percent), against a type-conditioned static prompt, a random-within-type control, a cached whole-binding-table prompt and an oracle, to claim that a query earns its cost only in proportion to the within-type, key-indexable variance the bank actually carries.
closest_prior_work: FocusMem, arXiv:2608.04530 (verified via s2cli, 2026-08-05): state-conditioned retrieval for GUI agents that is explicitly evaluated against 'a fully matched action-only fixed-memory baseline'. That matched fixed-memory control is precisely the comparison this proposal claims the literature never runs, so the framing sentence ('never as a function of what the query key can index... rarely over a fixed prompt') is already partly false in a preprint the proposal itself cites. FocusMem does not cross key type or manipulate how much state-keyed content the bank holds, so the rate ladder survives, but the 'nobody compares state-keyed retrieval to a matched static arm' premise does not. Two further verified neighbours narrow the gap: arXiv:2607.20972 (Delivery, Not Storage, verified, 2026-07-23) already argues that situationally-bound operational facts including locations must be cue-anchored to the current state rather than voluntarily retrieved by a task-level query, which is the qualitative content of P2; and arXiv:2608.04574 (When Memory Lies, verified, 2026-08-05) already shows that stale/incorrect spatial location memory produces navigation errors agents do not detect, which is the qualitative content of P4. Synapse arXiv:2306.07863 (verified, ICLR, 193 citations) established state abstraction as the exemplar key in 2023. So the mechanism is well-trodden; only the controlled plant rate is new.
strongest_objection: The two headline predictions are already decided by the node's own measurement that is printed inside the submission, and in opposite directions. The brief states, as a binding constraint, k3 - static3 = +17.2 net [+11.9, +22.4] on the natural bank. The proposal's r=0 goal-key cell IS that arm (its own Baselines section says 'goal-keyed top-3 retrieval (Measurement A, re-run at r=0)'). Therefore: (a) P1 ('at r=0 each key minus the best static arm lies within +/-8 net') is falsified before a single confirmatory cell runs, by data already in hand, which the proposal concedes in Risk Factors and then declines to act on; and (b) P2's confirmation threshold ('the observation-key residual reaches at least +13 net at r=1.0') is BELOW the already-measured r=0 residual of +17.2, so P2 is confirmed by doing nothing at all, and its second clause ('the goal-key residual stays within +/-8 net at every r') is false at r=0 by the same number. The brief's rule is explicit that residual predictions must be stated against the measured +17.2, not an assumed null; this proposal cites the rule and violates it. Everything downstream inherits the damage: P3's two equivalences and P4's gain term are measured against those same cells, and the abstract's thesis sentence ('a goal-keyed retriever cannot index anything a type-conditioned static prompt lacks') is a claim the node has already refuted by +17 points. Secondary but real: the plant is engineered so the retrieval side of P2 is true by construction (the binding item literally contains the scene signature the observation key is built from, and it is in the retrieval index), so the only open quantity in the headline experiment is whether a 32B reader acts on an explicitly supplied 30-token location fact - a demonstration, not a discovery - and the promised general rule is circular, since the 'bank statistic' is defined as the very residual it is supposed to predict and is never given a computable, pre-validated form.
what_would_fix_it: Re-anchor every prediction on the measured +17.2 and make the interaction, not the level, the claim. Concretely: (1) drop P1's containment claim and replace it with a decomposition of the existing +17.2 residual - what does the goal key deliver that three fixed type-matched exemplars do not (object-matched vs. type-matched exemplar ablation, exemplar count, on-policy vs. expert pool)? A proposal that cannot say why the goal key is already worth +17 has no standing to predict what a scene key adds. (2) Restate P2 as a pre-registered key x rate interaction contrast: (observation-key slope in r) minus (goal-key slope in r), each cell differenced against its own r=0 cell, with a cluster-bootstrap CI on the difference of slopes and a margin set as a fraction of +17.2 rather than of the Gate-0 +27/+32. Fix the P2 dead zone by making the confirmation and falsification thresholds the same number. State a falsifier for the asserted monotonicity or drop the word. (3) Add the wrong-scene, binding-shaped, length-matched placebo row so the control separates 'a binding-shaped item is present' from 'the scene-matched binding is present'; make P5 conditional on the r=1.0 observation-key increment first clearing the floor. (4) Strengthen the static comparator (see missing_baseline) so 'best static arm' is defensible. (5) Specify and log the stall key's firing rate and its base prompt, and report the stall arm on the subset where it fires as well as pooled. (6) Give the bank statistic a formula computable from the bank alone before any episode runs, and pre-register its predicted value for each of the four rates plus the natural level; validating that one number against the measured residuals is the only part of this design that would generalise beyond ALFWorld.
missing_baseline: A stronger static arm than static3. The whole claim is 'retrieval beats the BEST static prompt only when...', but the static comparator is three fixed type-conditioned exemplars (~430 tokens) plus a six-procedure type-agnostic prompt, and the measured residual over it is +17.2 - which is direct evidence that static3 is not the best static prompt. The brief demands compiled/many-shot static alternatives (G1, G3, G5); the proposal runs a whole-bank arm only for the artificial 274-row binding table and never for ordinary trajectory content. A many-shot static arm (e.g. 20-60 fixed expert exemplars, or a compiled per-type playbook distilled from the same pool, cached, at 4-8k tokens) at r=0 is the arm a reviewer will demand, because if it closes the +17.2 the paper's entire 'residual = key-indexable variance' story is measured against the wrong reference and the planted-binding ladder becomes an increment on top of an artefact of an under-powered baseline. Second omission, smaller: the wrong-scene binding-shaped placebo named above (the entailment check flags the same gap in P5).

COULD NOT VERIFY arXiv:2506.03989 (cited as motivating the cached whole-table arm; 'not found on S2 or HF' - the id should be corrected or dropped). Judgement of the proposal's own check: it is one of the better collision checks I have seen in this round - it names its channel, lists queries by class including a home-vocabulary query without agent/memory words, gives IDs, and correctly identifies FocusMem as the nearest live threat. Two faults: it under-weights what it found (FocusMem's 'fully matched fixed-memory baseline' contradicts the proposal's own 'never compared against a matched static arm' premise), and it missed arXiv:2607.20972 and arXiv:2608.04574, which pre-empt the qualitative content of P2 and P4 respectively and were reachable from the proposal's own vocabulary.
